description: Hi everyone! We’re forming a team for the Space Mission Design Game challenge. We’re passionate about space exploration, game development, and creating engaging, educational experiences that make complex aerospace concepts accessible and fun.
summary: We developed MARGIN // HELIOS-4, an interactive 3D space mission design and aerospace systems engineering simulation game built with Godot 4 (WebGL 2.0). Addressing the challenge, our game puts players in the seat of a NASA Mission Director tasked with building a modular spacecraft across five hardware slots (Core Bus, Propulsion, Solar Array, Thermal Shield, and Science Instruments) for missions to Sun-Earth L1, the Lunar South Pole, or Mars. Every part selection dynamically updates coupled physical equations—including Tsiolkovsky Delta-V, Launch Thrust-to-Weight Ratio (TWR), inverse-square solar power, and thermal flux—across five live engineering margin gauges. Players pass a Flight Readiness Review, pilot a guided polar gravity-turn launch to a 185 km parking orbit, survive Coronal Mass Ejection (CME) solar storms, and deploy 3D space-weather instruments. This project is important because it transforms complex NASA systems engineering trade-offs into an accessible, hands-on browser simulation for students and aspiring engineers.
details:
WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS:

MARGIN // HELIOS-4 is an interactive 3D space mission design and aerospace systems engineering simulation game. Players step into the shoes of a NASA Mission Director to design a modular spacecraft across 5 hardware slots (Core Bus, Propulsion Stage, Solar Array/Battery, Thermal Shield, and Science Payload) or select the NASA Baseline Preset. Every part change dynamically updates coupled physical equations—including Tsiolkovsky Delta-V, Launch Thrust-to-Weight Ratio (TWR), inverse-square solar power balance, and thermal flux—displayed across 5 live engineering margin gauges. After passing a Flight Readiness Review (FRR), players pilot a guided polar gravity-turn launch to a 185 km parking orbit, survive Coronal Mass Ejection (CME) solar storms in deep space, and commission space-weather instruments at Sun-Earth L1, the Moon, or Mars.

BENEFITS & INTENDED IMPACT:

The project transforms complex NASA systems engineering trade-offs into an intuitive, gamified learning experience. It helps students, space enthusiasts, and aspiring engineers understand that space missions succeed not just by raw power, but by rigorously balancing mass, propellant, power, and thermal margins.

TOOLS, LANGUAGES & SOFTWARE USED:

- Game Engine: Godot 4 (Exported to WebGL 2.0 / HTML5 WebAssembly)

- Programming Language: Strongly-typed GDScript

- Audio: Zero-dependency Procedural WebGL Audio Synthesizer (AudioStreamGenerator) for real-time engine roars, RCS, and CME klaxon alarms

- Deployment & Version Control: Vercel Edge CDN & GitHub

- AI Assistance: Google Gemini & OpenAI Codex / Antigravity for systems architecture planning, mathematical verification, and code refactoring.

CREATIVITY & FACTORS CONSIDERED:

Unlike standard quizzes or passive videos, our game couples real orbital mechanics (polar gravity-turn kinematics and inverse-square solar irradiance) directly with interactive 3D gameplay. We factored in real NASA FRR gate criteria, allowing players to either fix engineering deficits in the hangar or issue a Flight Director Waiver with explicit operational risks that impact final mission debrief scoring.
